question: Which of the following dances means ‘dance of the enchantress’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohiniyattam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form from the state of Kerala, India.
 
• The term "Mohiniyattam" means "dance of the enchantress," derived from the word "Mohini," a mythical enchantress avatar of the Hindu god Vishnu.
 
• It is characterized by graceful, swaying body movements, subtle facial expressions, and simple but elegant costumes.
 
• This dance form primarily narrates themes of love and devotion, often drawing from both Hindu mythology and folk stories.
 
• Mohiniyattam is traditionally performed as a solo recital by women.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Origin and History**

 
 
• Mohiniyattam is believed to have originated during the 16th century under the patronage of the Chera kings of Kerala.
 
• The dance form received a significant revival in the 19th century under the rule of Swathi Thirunal, a king of Travancore, who was an ardent lover of arts.
 
 
 
• **Costume and Makeup**
 
 
• The traditional costume for Mohiniyattam includes a white or off-white sari with golden borders, known as Kasavu sari.
 
• Performers wear minimal makeup with special emphasis on the eyes to highlight expressions, and their hair is typically styled in a bun adorned with jasmine flowers.
 
 
 
• **Music and Instruments**
 
 
• The accompanying music for Mohiniyattam is Carnatic, which is the classical music tradition of South India.
 
• Key instruments used include the Mridangam, Veena, Idakka, and Edakka.
 
 
 
• **Performance Structure**
 
 
• A typical Mohiniyattam performance includes several stages such as Cholkettu, Varnam, Padam, and Thillana, each with its own unique features and significance.
 
• Each stage of the performance is designed to showcase the dancer's skills in abhinaya (expression) and footwork.
